Contract law - formation
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties.
Essentials: offer, acceptance, consideration, intention to create legal relations
offer = a definite promise to be bound on specific terms
invitation to treat is an invitation to make an offer, e.g. goods on a shop shelf (Pharmaceutical Society v Boots)
acceptance must be unconditional + communicated (mirror image rule)
postal rule: acceptance is complete when the letter is posted (Adams v Lindsell 1818)
consideration is something of value given in exchange for a promise
past consideration is not good consideration (Re McArdle)
